To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of catabolism of cAMP by cAMP-dependent protein kinases from rabbit skeletal muscle, in vitro, is controlled by a dynamic equilibrium between a ternary complex and its constituent dissociable species.
the rate of dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits is slow in the absence of C but becomes very rapid in the presence of C and MgATP, suggesting that the regulatory subunit-cAM...
in the absence of catalytic subunit, the dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits is a slow process, whereas in the presence of catalytic subunits, the dissociation is a very rapid process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetic studies of the dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits of cAMP-dependent kinase, type I.
the kinetic studies on the dissociaton of adenosine 5'-cyclic phosphate (cAMP) from the regulatory subunits of protein kinase from skeletal muscle.
the kinetic studies on the activation of cAMP-dependent kinase from rabbit skeletal by the catalytic subunits of the enzyme and by the regulatory subunits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of catabolism of cAMP in the regulatory subunit-cyclic nucleotide complex is not a limiting factor in the regulation of cAMP-dependent kinase activity by changes in the cellular levels of cAMP.
the catalytic subunits of cAMP-dependent kinase are responsible for the dissociation of the regulatory subunit-cyclic AMP complex.

the catalysis of the dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits of cAMP-dependent kinase, type I is a catalytic function of the catalytic (C) subunits and that this catalysis is MgATP-dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulatory subunit-cyclic 3',5'AMP complex is a dynamic entity and is subject to a rapid exchange of the cAMP molecule with its environment, and that the rate of this exchange is markedly affected by the presence and absence of the catalytical subunit and MgATP.
the rate enhancement of the dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits by C is the rate limiting step in the activation of protein kinase.
the dissociation of cAMP from the regulatory subunits of cAMP-dependent kinase is a slow process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic subunits can bind to regulatory subunits with cAMP bound in either a slow or a fast process.
the rate of catabolism of cAMP from the regulatory subunits is not the limiting factor in the regulation of the activity of cAMP-dependent kinase in vivo.
cAMP-dependent protein kinases are not simply "switches" that are turned on or off by cAMP.
